notes: Tasks are ordered by dependency and intended for direct implementation in the development-sandbox-env worktree.
The current worktree branch is development-sandbox-env, which does not satisfy the repository preflight rule requiring feature/<slug>.

tasks.title: Create sandbox asset skeleton
tasks.description: Add the new sandbox asset directory and the baseline files required by the spec. Keep the file layout minimal and focused on local Docker sandbox lifecycle only.
acceptance: The infra/sandbox directory exists with the four expected files.
The README explains the sandbox purpose and points users to make sandbox-start and make sandbox-destroy.
The env template lists only GitHub/OpenAI-related host secrets as required or optional inputs.

tasks.title: Build the sandbox image from pinned tool versions
tasks.description: Implement the Docker image so it installs Python 3.13.5, Node.js 22.21.0, pnpm 9.15.1, gh, PostgreSQL server/client tooling, Codex CLI, Playwright, Chromium dependencies, SSH tooling, and the common CLI utilities the repository scripts rely on. Structure the Dockerfile for cache-friendly incremental rebuilds by keeping stable OS, runtime, and global CLI installation in early layers, copying sandbox scripts late, and not copying the repository into the image.
acceptance: The Dockerfile uses .tool-versions as the source of truth for Python, Node.js, and pnpm versions.

The Dockerfile is organized for cache-friendly rebuilds: apt or system packages, language runtimes, and global CLI installs live in stable early layers, while sandbox scripts and config are copied in later layers.
The repository source tree is not copied into the image; the repo is cloned at container startup into the persistent workspace volume.
The built image provides jq, python, node, pnpm, gh, make, git, codex, psql, pg_isready, and playwright on PATH.
The image creates a non-root agent user suitable for SSH and VS Code Remote-SSH.

tasks.title: Implement idempotent container bootstrap
tasks.description: Implement the container entrypoint so each sandbox initializes and starts SSH and PostgreSQL, creates the local app database and role if missing, exports DATABASE_URL and OpenAI variables into login shells, configures gh auth from GH_TOKEN, and clones the repository on first boot only.
acceptance: A first boot initializes PostgreSQL data, starts sshd, authenticates gh from GH_TOKEN, and clones the repo to /workspace/webclippings.
A later boot reuses the existing home, workspace, and database state without recloning or dropping data.
The sandbox shell environment exposes DATABASE_URL for the local Postgres instance and preserves OpenAI env vars for SSH and VS Code sessions.
Changing sandbox bootstrap scripts only invalidates late Docker layers and does not require reinstalling the full toolchain unless the runtime installation steps themselves changed.

tasks.title: Add instance-aware sandbox lifecycle Make targets
tasks.description: Add exactly two user-facing targets, make sandbox-start name=<id> and make sandbox-destroy name=<id>. Derive deterministic container names, volumes, SSH ports, web ports, and host export directories from the instance id.
acceptance: make help documents sandbox-start and sandbox-destroy.
sandbox-start builds or reuses the image, creates the required resources, and prints SSH, VS Code, web URL, repo path, and extension export path.
sandbox-destroy removes only the named container, its instance-specific volumes, and its host export directory while leaving the image cached.

tasks.title: Wire host-visible web and extension access
tasks.description: Publish one host web port per sandbox and provide a per-instance host export directory for the unpacked Chrome extension. Keep source editing inside the sandbox and expose only the built extension artifacts to the host.
acceptance: The backend can bind to 0.0.0.0 inside the sandbox and be reached from the host at the printed localhost URL.
Each sandbox gets a host-visible extension export directory under .local/sandboxes/<id>/exports/extension.
The README documents that the host browser opens the web app and host Chrome loads the exported unpacked extension.

tasks.title: Document sandbox operating model and recovery behavior
tasks.description: Document the required host secrets, SSH assumptions, multi-instance naming model, expected lifecycle commands, idempotent restart behavior, and cleanup/recovery path when sandbox startup fails or ports collide.
acceptance: The README documents required host env vars as OPENAI_API_KEY and GH_TOKEN only, with the OpenAI optional variables listed separately.
The README explains how to connect with SSH and VS Code Remote-SSH and how to open the web app and extension outputs from the host.
The README describes failure handling for reruns, port collisions, and make sandbox-destroy cleanup.

tasks.title: Validate single-sandbox readiness
tasks.description: Start one sandbox instance and verify the image contents, SSH access, VS Code compatibility, local PostgreSQL wiring, backend reachability, and extension export behavior from end to end.
acceptance: make sandbox-start name=alpha succeeds and prints connection details.
Inside alpha, python --version, node --version, pnpm --version, gh auth status, codex --version, and pg_isready succeed with the expected toolchain.
The host can open the alpha web URL and see the app after make all-init and make all-run in the sandbox.
pnpm run build:worktree in the sandbox produces a host-visible unpacked extension export for alpha.

tasks.title: Validate multi-sandbox isolation
tasks.description: Run at least two sandbox instances in parallel and verify deterministic isolation across container names, ports, volumes, PostgreSQL state, and host extension export paths.
acceptance: make sandbox-start name=alpha and make sandbox-start name=beta can run concurrently.
Alpha and beta have different SSH ports, web ports, volumes, and extension export directories.
Destroying alpha leaves beta intact and usable.

tasks.title: Capture deferred cleanup as tech debt if needed
tasks.description: If implementation reveals follow-up work that is intentionally deferred, especially around version drift between .tool-versions, CI, and existing docs, record it explicitly in the tech debt backlog.
acceptance: Any deferred cleanup discovered during implementation is captured in docs/TECH_DEBT_BACKLOG.md with concrete next steps.
No backlog item is added if no real deferred work remains.
